quotes.text: Orchestration is in private preview. [Share your email address to request access.](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/orchestration.md#orchestration_preview)
For payments routed to third-party processors, those processors administer the refunds.
All related activity (including payment processing fees and liability for transaction losses) remain subject to the terms that you agreed to with that processor.
Orchestration also doesn’t support disputes or settlement-related activity.

findings: Both overviews describe rule-based card payment routing with PaymentIntents or configured auto-created PaymentIntents from Billing, Checkout, Payment Links and Dashboard payments, alternative processor retry, performance monitoring and testing in sandbox before live activation. Payments, Billing and Dashboard payments are named in the supported product list (old raw lines 12–37; new raw lines 25–49).

The separate route guide lines 27–54 and 74–86 narrows prerequisites to representative-led account onboarding, compatible destination processor and integration, destination credentials provided in Dashboard, activated rules, server-side PaymentIntent opt-in via `payments_orchestration[enabled]=true` for the illustrated flow, and representative configuration for supported auto-created PaymentIntents. Sandbox and live activation are separate (lines 39–48 and 208–210). No API version change or successful onboarding is shown by the overview.

The overview keeps Stripe Dashboard/Refunds API as initiation and management surfaces, while the routed third party remains processor of record, administers its refunds, retains fees and liability under its own terms, and supplies the dashboard for disputes/settlement-related activity (old raw lines 25–39, new raw lines 37–51). The feature guide describes preemptive refund on `processing` as submission after payment success or failing the refund request if payment fails (line 55). The route guide lines 84–91 and 114–132 separates PaymentIntent state and the Payment Record/attempt history from Stripe Charges and Balance Transactions on third-party volume. Preview request, rule activation, routing, retry and refund initiation are distinct from payment success, refund completion and settlement.

The November overview line 51 excludes Link and non-card payments. The implementation guide lines 35–37 clarifies Link transactions stay with Stripe and are excluded from routing rules because credentials cannot transfer. This is distinct from Apple Pay and Google Pay routing in the feature matrix lines 35–53 and wallet guide lines 23–38, which carries processor, DPAN/FPAN and 3DS constraints. Saved mobile wallets use `off_session=true` during PaymentIntent confirmation; a present customer must be re-prompted through the wallet integration.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/orchestration, both complete captures describe private-preview, rule-based card payment routing across Stripe-supported processors. November adds an email request form with the `orchestration_preview` registration key. It requests access. The separately documented implementation requires representative onboarding, supported processor and integration checks, destination credentials, configured rules and separate live activation. PaymentIntents can opt in server-side. Billing, Checkout, Payment Links and Dashboard can use configured auto-created PaymentIntents. Rules can retry eligible failures, and Dashboard monitoring and sandbox testing precede live activation (old raw lines 8-37 and new raw lines 9-49). The third-party processor still processes routed payments, retains contractual fees and liability, administers refunds initiated via the Stripe Dashboard or Refunds API, and handles disputes and settlement activity outside Orchestration. Non-card payments, Link, Capital, Connect, Terminal and Organizations are excluded. May also explicitly excluded Radar on third-party routed payments and Sigma. November omits those names (old raw lines 25-39 and new raw lines 37-51). The mapped `source-stripe-orchestration.md` accurately carries the core May features and processor-of-record boundaries, with the May exclusions undated in the body and the new request route absent. Access request, activated rule, processor attempt and refund initiation each have their own documented state. These states do not establish paid, refunded or settled status.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/orchestration, the documented email-based private-preview request and the narrower exclusion wording are substantive documentation changes (old raw lines 8-10 and 31-39, new raw lines 9-23 and 43-51). Heading whitespace, collection metadata and anchor placement are presentational or navigational. Preserve the May-specific Radar-on-third-party and Sigma exclusions in `source-stripe-orchestration.md` line 29 and the reciprocal Orchestration concept line 39. November’s omission establishes no support change. Separately, the retry guide says a Radar block when Stripe is main processor is treated as a decline subject to retry, alongside no retry after failed main-processor 3DS or for an ineligible retry feature. Carry the Stripe-main predicate into the linked retries source and qualify the index shorthand about Radar blocks. Link stays on Stripe outside routing rules. Separately, Apple Pay and Google Pay have processor and wallet qualifications, including `off_session=true` for saved mobile wallets and re-prompting present customers. The registration POST is a documentation access form. The separate implementation guide qualifies server-created `payments_orchestration` PaymentIntents, configuration for automatically created intents, sandbox versus live rule activation, and Payment Records and Stripe balance reporting by actual processor. The overview gives no changed API or SDK version requirement. Stripe’s refund entry points do not transfer third-party processor responsibilities or prove processing, refund or settlement outcomes (old raw lines 19-39 and new raw lines 31-51).
